Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in Michigan, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Ask for your ballot by

Friday, October 30Passed

Online and mailed applications must reach your local clerk by 5 p.m. on the Friday before Election Day: Friday, October 30, 2026. If you are registered at your current address, you can apply in person at your clerk's office until 4 p.m. on Monday, November 2, 2026. If you need to register or update your address, you can do it at the clerk's office and vote an absentee ballot there until 8 p.m. on Election Day. The state suggests applying at least 15 days ahead to leave time for the mail; that suggested date has passed, so think about returning your ballot in person or by drop box. (official page)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

Your local clerk must receive your ballot by 8 p.m. on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Ballots that arrive later are not counted (military and overseas voters have a later deadline). (official page)

The last day to ask for a ballot by mail has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. Early voting in person runs through Sunday, November 1, 2026. When and where to vote early.

Ask for a ballot online, on Michigan’s own site

At school away from home, in Michigan or in another state? What Michigan says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

No reason is needed. Every registered Michigan voter has the right to vote by mail with an absentee ballot. You must apply first, unless you are on the permanent absentee ballot list (a box on the application), which sends you a ballot for every election. (official page)

How to ask for a ballot

  • Online. Apply at Michigan.gov/Vote. You need your Michigan driver's license or state ID number (or to say you have none), the last four digits of your Social Security number, and an uploaded signature or permission to use the signature the Secretary of State already has. Open it (official page)
  • By mail. Print an absentee ballot application (or pick one up at your city or township clerk's office), sign it, and mail it to your local clerk, put it in one of the clerk's drop boxes, or drop it off at the clerk's office. Open it (official page)
  • In person. Go to your city or township clerk's office to apply, and you can fill out and turn in your ballot right there. If you are not registered at your current Michigan address, you can register (with proof of where you live) and get an absentee ballot at the clerk's office up to 8 p.m. on Election Day. (official page)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Mail it in the pre-paid return envelope; no stamp is needed. The state does not recommend mailing within 14 days of the election, since it must arrive by 8 p.m. on Election Day. (official page)
  • Drop box. Put it in one of your own city's or township's secure drop boxes by 8 p.m. on Election Day. The state's page points voters to their own clerk's drop boxes in their own city or township. Find your clerk's drop boxes at Michigan.gov/Vote. (official page)
  • In person. Hand it in at your local clerk's office by 8 p.m. on Election Day. You can also bring it to your early voting site (through Sunday, November 1) or your polling place on Election Day and put it into the ballot counter yourself (Detroit voters cannot do this at polling places). Only you, a member of your immediate family, or someone who lives in your household may deliver it for you, if you ask them; it is a felony for anyone else to hold or deliver your ballot. (official page)

What the envelope needs

No witness or notary is needed. Sign and date the return envelope using the signature on your driver's license, state ID or voter registration; the clerk compares it to the signature on file. If the signature is found not to match, the ballot is rejected and the clerk must tell you promptly. A paper application also needs your signature of record; an online one asks for your license or ID number and the last four digits of your Social Security number. (official page)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on Michigan’s own site

See when your clerk mailed your ballot and when it came back at Michigan.gov/Vote. You can also sign up there for status messages. (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Saturday, October 24, 2026 to Sunday, November 1, 2026.

Every community offers at least nine days of early voting, from the second Saturday before Election Day through the Sunday before: Saturday, October 24 through Sunday, November 1, 2026. Some communities start earlier (as early as 29 days before) or add Monday, November 2. You must vote at your assigned early voting site; look it up at Michigan.gov/Vote. Bring photo ID if you have one; without it you can sign a statement and still vote. (official page)

Students

At school in Michigan, away from home

Michigan's Department of State says students choose whether to register at their school address or at their permanent hometown address, and may change it back whenever they choose. Registering at a school address also changes the address on a Michigan driver's license or state ID. A student who keeps their hometown address can vote with an absentee ballot. Students registered at their campus address can request and turn in an absentee ballot at the local clerk's office or an on-campus satellite office. Within 14 days of an election, registering or changing your address must be done in person at the local clerk's office with proof of residence, which can include a school document or a school web portal page showing your name and campus address. (official page)

At school in another state, with Michigan as home

Michigan's Department of State says Michigan students who keep a permanent home address in Michigan while attending school in another state can vote in Michigan with an absentee ballot. They may instead register and vote at their out-of-state campus address if that state allows it, but may vote in only one state in an election. Students from other states going to school in Michigan may register at their Michigan campus address. A student studying abroad can vote as an overseas voter. (official page)

Military and overseas

Military and overseas voters can ask for a ballot by email, fax or mail with the Federal Post Card Application or Michigan's own application; to be sure of a ballot, the application should reach the clerk by 2 p.m. Saturday, October 31, 2026. A mailed ballot must be postmarked by Election Day, November 3, and received within 6 days after (by Monday, November 9, 2026). Uniformed service members may return a ballot online by 8 p.m. on Election Day if their application carried their Common Access Card signature. (federal guide)

Michigan in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • You can register to vote in Michigan up to and on Election Day, in person at your city or township clerk's office, with proof of where you live.
  • If you have an absentee ballot and decide to vote in person instead, you can bring it to your early voting site or polling place and either put it in the counter or give it up and get a new ballot, as long as you have not already returned it.
  • If you returned your ballot and want to change your vote, a written, signed request must reach your clerk by 5 p.m. on the second Friday before Election Day (Friday, October 23, 2026).
  • Voters with print disabilities can ask for an accessible ballot that is emailed and can be marked on their own device.
  • Polls on Election Day close at 8 p.m.; anyone in line by then may vote.
